manual.mchjong.entry.automatic_table.int: An automatic mahjong table shuffles, builds the wall, deals and draws by itself, and assigns seats directly. MCR, Sichuan mahjong and Taiwanese mahjong are played only on automatic tables; Riichi mahjong can use either kind.
manual.mchjong.entry.automatic_table.upg: Craft an automatic mahjong table by arranging an ordinary mahjong table and the other materials as follows:$(li)Top row: iron ingot, redstone dust, iron ingot$(li)Middle row: redstone dust, mahjong table, redstone dust$(li)Bottom row: copper ingot, hopper, copper ingot
The mahjong table used in the recipe must be empty. The automatic mahjong table keeps its original wood and name.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.declare: In Riichi mahjong, click Riichi while in tenpai and then click a highlighted tile to discard it and declare riichi. In Taiwanese mahjong, click Declare Ready and discard a highlighted tile to declare ready. Right-click or press Esc before discarding to cancel.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.discard: On your turn, click a tile in your hand to discard it. Under Discard Input in personal settings, choose Single Click or Double Click.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.discard.co: When you can chi, pon, kan or win, buttons appear beside your hand. Click a button to choose the action, then click the tiles to use if there is more than one combination. Click Pass to decline. Right-click or press Esc to cancel the current selection.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.name: Table Controls
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.view: The view button on the toolbar switches between Seated View and Immersive View. Hold the right mouse button and drag to look around, and scroll to zoom. Personal settings adjust the camera distance and height and can reset the view direction.
manual.mchjong.entry.controls.view.conti: To leave your seat, press Esc to close the table screen and then press the sneak key.
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.name: Personal Settings
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.packs: Custom tile faces, backs, riichi sticks and voices can be packaged as ZIP presets in the faces, backs, sticks and voices folders under config/mchjong/presets in the game directory. Joining a server with preset sharing enabled downloads its presets automatically.
manual.mchjong.entry.customization.setti: Click Settings on the toolbar, select Personal on the left, then open Personal Settings to adjust the view, table animations, discard input, hand and river display, and effect and voice volumes. Personal Presets, in the same category, selects the riichi-stick appearance and match voice.
The host manages the settings in the Room category. Only operators can change the settings in the World category.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.cloth: A mahjong table needs a table cloth before a match can start. Hold the cloth, aim at the table and press Use (right-click by default) to lay it. Any previous cloth returns to your inventory. To retrieve the cloth, aim at the tabletop with an empty hand, hold Sneak and press Use.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.cloth.con: When no match is in progress, use the table with an empty hand or a mahjong box to open the table’s storage. Put boxes of tiles there, and the table selects a set from them when the match starts. The cloth and storage cannot be changed during a match.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.manual: With Patchouli installed, each player receives a Mahjong Manual on first joining a world. Craft another from a book, green dye and one mahjong tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.name: Setting Up a Table
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.placement: A mahjong table needs a 3×3 clear area. The block directly below the center must be solid, and the nine spaces and the layer above them must be free of blocks and liquids.
Place a mahjong stool at the middle of each side where a player will sit, two blocks from the table’s center. A four-player match needs four stools; three-player mahjong needs three.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.recipes: Craft a mahjong table from five slabs and two fences of the same wood. The table keeps that wood.
manual.mchjong.entry.furniture.recipes.c: Craft two mahjong stools from two slabs, two fences and two carpets of one color; the seats match the carpet color.$(br2)Three carpets of one color in a row make a table cloth of that color.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.collect: After a hand ends and point sticks have been paid, push your tiles to the middle of the table to continue to the next hand.$(br2)When the match ends and the table returns to the lobby, the dice and the sticks in the drawers are collected automatically.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.deal: To deal, drag the highlighted part of the wall into your hand. Each player takes four tiles three times and then one more; the dealer takes a fourteenth tile and discards first.$(br2)During play, drag the highlighted wall tile into your hand when it is your turn to draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.manual: When Riichi mahjong is played on an ordinary table, players shuffle, build the wall, break it and take their tiles by hand. Tiles to move are highlighted, and the prompt at the top of the screen describes the current step. Press Esc to cancel a drag.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.manual.con: $(li)Shuffle: drag the face-down tiles on the tabletop.$(li)Build: drag highlighted tiles in front of you to form your wall.$(li)Break: once the walls are built, the dealer picks up the dice in the middle of the table, rolls them and breaks the wall at the result.
manual.mchjong.entry.handling.name: Manual Table Handling
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.maid: With Touhou Little Maid installed, you can set a maid’s job to Mahjong.
manual.mchjong.entry.maid.maid.continued: Prepare a mahjong table with a cloth within her work area, leave an empty stool, and take a seat first. During working hours, she walks to the empty stool and sits down, then takes her assigned seat when the match starts. Changing her job makes her stand up at once and free the seat.

manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.all_ev: $(bold)All Even Pungs$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) and the pair only of 2, 4, 6 and 8. Not counted: All Pungs, All Simples, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.all_gr: $(bold)All Green$()$(br)88 points$(br2)Only 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 of Bamboo and Green. Full Flush or Half Flush can also count.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.all_ho: $(bold)All Honors$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Only honors. Not counted: All Pungs, Outside Hand, Pung of Terminals or Honors, One Voided Suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.all_te: $(bold)All Terminals$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Only 1s and 9s. Not counted: All Pungs, Outside Hand, Pung of Terminals or Honors, No Honors. A separate Double Pung can count.
$(bold)All Terminals and Honors$()$(br)32 points$(br2)Only 1s, 9s and honors. Not counted: All Pungs, Outside Hand, Pung of Terminals or Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.big_fo: $(bold)Big Four Winds$()$(br)88 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of East, South, West and North. Not counted: Big Three Winds, Prevalent Wind, Seat Wind, Pung of Terminals or Honors, All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.big_th: $(bold)Big Three Dragons$()$(br)88 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of Red, Green and White. Not counted: Two Dragon Pungs, Dragon Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.four_c: $(bold)Four Concealed Pungs$()$(br)64 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Four concealed pungs (including concealed kongs); a pung completed with another player’s discard is not concealed. Not counted: All Pungs, Concealed Hand. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.four_k: $(bold)Four Kongs$()$(br)88 points$(br2)Four kongs and a pair. Not counted: Single Wait. Concealed kongs still count Concealed Kong, Two Concealed Kongs or concealed-pung patterns by number.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.four_p: $(bold)Four Pure Shifted Chows$()$(br)32 points$(br2)Four chows in one suit whose starting numbers rise by one or by two. Three of them do not count Pure Shifted Chows.
$(bold)Four Pure Shifted Pungs$()$(br)48 points$(br2)Four pungs in one suit, each number one higher. Not counted: Pure Shifted Pungs, All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.full_f: $(bold)Full Flush$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Only one suit, with no honors. Not counted: One Voided Suit, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.greate: $(bold)Greater Honors and Knitted Tiles$()$(br)24 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)One of each of the seven honors plus seven tiles from 147, 258 and 369 in three different suits, fourteen different tiles. Not counted: Lesser Honors and Knitted Tiles, All Types, Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.intro: The value shown for each pattern is its own point value, not the total hand score. Patterns listed as not counted are not added again. See $(l:mcr_special)Hands and Combining$(/l) for the rules on combining patterns.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.little: $(bold)Little Four Winds$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of three winds with the fourth wind as the pair. Not counted: Big Three Winds; the three wind sets do not count Pung of Terminals or Honors.
$(bold)Little Three Dragons$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of two dragons with the third dragon as the pair. Not counted: Two Dragon Pungs, Dragon Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.lower_: $(bold)Lower Tiles$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Only 1, 2 and 3. Not counted: Lower Four, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.middle: $(bold)Middle Tiles$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Only 4, 5 and 6. Not counted: All Simples, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.name: 88 to 24 Points
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.nine_g: $(bold)Nine Gates$()$(br)88 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)1112345678999 of one suit, winning on any tile of that suit. Not counted: Full Flush, Concealed Hand. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.pure_s: $(bold)Pure Shifted Pungs$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Three pungs in one suit, each number one higher. They do not count Pure Triple Chow.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.pure_t: $(bold)Pure Terminal Chows$()$(br)64 points$(br2)Two each of 123 and 789 in one suit, with the 5 of that suit as the pair. Not counted: Full Flush, All Chows, Pure Double Chow, Two Terminal Chows, No Honors.
$(bold)Pure Triple Chow$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Three identical chows in one suit. They do not count Pure Shifted Pungs or Pure Double Chow.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.quadru: $(bold)Quadruple Chow$()$(br)48 points$(br2)Four identical chows in one suit. Not counted: Pure Triple Chow, Pure Double Chow, Tile Hog.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.seven_: $(bold)Seven Pairs$()$(br)24 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Seven pairs; four identical tiles may form two pairs and add Tile Hog. Not counted: Concealed Hand, Single Wait. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.

$(bold)Seven Shifted Pairs$()$(br)88 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Seven pairs of consecutive numbers in one suit. Not counted: Seven Pairs, Full Flush, Concealed Hand, Single Wait. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.thirte: $(bold)Thirteen Orphans$()$(br)88 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)One of each terminal and honor plus a second copy of one as the pair. Adds Fully Concealed Hand when self-drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.three_: $(bold)Three Kongs$()$(br)32 points$(br2)Three kongs. Concealed kongs still count Concealed Kong or Two Concealed Kongs; if all three are concealed, Three Concealed Pungs also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_high.upper_: $(bold)Upper Tiles$()$(br)24 points$(br2)Only 7, 8 and 9. Not counted: Upper Four, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.all_cho: $(bold)All Chows$()$(br)2 points$(br2)All four melds are chows and the pair is a suited tile. Not counted: No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.all_sim: $(bold)All Simples$()$(br)2 points$(br2)Only 2 to 8, with no 1s, 9s or honors. Not counted: No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.closed_: $(bold)Closed Wait$()$(br)1 point$(br2)The only win is the middle tile of a chow. Not counted if the hand can win another way. Only one of Edge Wait, Closed Wait and Single Wait counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.conceal: $(bold)Concealed Hand$()$(br)2 points$(br2)Win on another player's discard without having called a chow, pung or melded kong. Concealed kongs are allowed. A self-drawn win with a concealed hand scores Fully Concealed Hand instead; Concealed Hand is not counted.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.double_: $(bold)Double Pung$()$(br)2 points$(br2)Two pungs (including kongs) of the same number in different suits.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.dragon_: $(bold)Dragon Pung$()$(br)2 points$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of Red, Green or White.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.edge_wa: $(bold)Edge Wait$()$(br)1 point$(br2)The only win is a 3 completing 123 or a 7 completing 789. Not counted if the hand can win another way. Only one of Edge Wait, Closed Wait and Single Wait counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.flower_: $(bold)Flower Tiles$()$(br)1 point per flower$(br2)Each revealed flower scores 1 point. Flower points do not count toward the 8-point minimum.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.fully_c: $(bold)Fully Concealed Hand$()$(br)4 points$(br2)Win by self-draw with a concealed hand. Concealed kongs keep the hand concealed. Not counted: Concealed Hand, Self-Drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.intro: The value shown for each pattern is its own point value, not the total hand score. Patterns listed as not counted are not added again. See $(l:mcr_special)Hands and Combining$(/l) for the rules on combining patterns.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.last_ti: $(bold)Last Tile$()$(br)4 points$(br2)Win on the fourth copy of a tile when the other three are already visible. Tiles hidden in other hands or in the wall are not visible.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.melded_: $(bold)Melded Kong$()$(br)1 point$(br2)One melded kong: a kong on another player’s discard, or a tile added to a melded pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.mixed_d: $(bold)Mixed Double Chow$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Two chows of the same numbers in different suits.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.name: 4 to 1 Points
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.no_hono: $(bold)No Honors$()$(br)1 point$(br2)The hand has no honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.one_voi: $(bold)One Voided Suit$()$(br)1 point$(br2)One of Characters, Circles and Bamboo is missing from the hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.outside: $(bold)Outside Hand$()$(br)4 points$(br2)Every meld and the pair include a 1, a 9 or an honor.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.prevale: $(bold)Prevalent Wind$()$(br)2 points$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of the prevalent wind. Seat Wind also counts when it is the same wind. This set does not count Pung of Terminals or Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.pung_of: $(bold)Pung of Terminals or Honors$()$(br)1 point$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of 1s or 9s, or of a wind that is neither the prevalent nor your seat wind. Dragon pungs count Dragon Pung instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.pure_do: $(bold)Pure Double Chow$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Two identical chows in one suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.seat_wi: $(bold)Seat Wind$()$(br)2 points$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of your seat wind. Prevalent Wind also counts when it is the same wind. This set does not count Pung of Terminals or Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.self_dr: $(bold)Self-Drawn$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Win on a tile you draw yourself.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.short_s: $(bold)Short Straight$()$(br)1 point$(br2)Two chows of one suit that join into six consecutive numbers.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.single_: $(bold)Single Wait$()$(br)1 point$(br2)The only win is one tile completing the pair. Not counted if the hand can win another way. Only one of Edge Wait, Closed Wait and Single Wait counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.tile_ho: $(bold)Tile Hog$()$(br)2 points$(br2)All four copies of one tile are used in the hand without forming a kong. Counts once for each such tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.two_con: $(bold)Two Concealed Pungs$()$(br)2 points$(br2)Two concealed pungs (including concealed kongs); a pung completed with another player’s discard is not concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.two_mel: $(bold)Two Melded Kongs$()$(br)4 points$(br2)Two melded kongs. One melded and one concealed kong score 6 points instead. Neither counts Melded Kong or Concealed Kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_low.two_ter: $(bold)Two Terminal Chows$()$(br)1 point$(br2)A 123 chow and a 789 chow of the same suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.all_: $(bold)All Fives$()$(br)16 points$(br2)Every meld and the pair include a 5. Not counted: All Simples, No Honors.
$(bold)All Pungs$()$(br)6 points$(br2)Four pungs (including kongs) and a pair.
$(bold)All Types$()$(br)6 points$(br2)The hand includes Characters, Circles, Bamboo, winds and dragons.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.big_: $(bold)Big Three Winds$()$(br)12 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of three winds. They do not count Pung of Terminals or Honors, but Prevalent Wind and Seat Wind still count when they apply.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.chic: $(bold)Chicken Hand$()$(br)8 points$(br2)A win with no scoring pattern other than flowers. Flower points are added separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.half: $(bold)Half Flush$()$(br)6 points$(br2)Only one suit plus honors. Not counted: One Voided Suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.intr: The value shown for each pattern is its own point value, not the total hand score. Patterns listed as not counted are not added again. See $(l:mcr_special)Hands and Combining$(/l) for the rules on combining patterns.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.knit: $(bold)Knitted Straight$()$(br)12 points$(br2)The nine tiles 147, 258 and 369 in three different suits, plus one meld and a pair. Only that meld may be melded. The nine tiles cannot be regrouped for other patterns.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.last: $(bold)Last Tile Claim$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Win on the discard made after another player draws the last tile of the wall.
$(bold)Last Tile Draw$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Win by drawing the last tile of the wall. Not counted: Self-Drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.less: $(bold)Lesser Honors and Knitted Tiles$()$(br)12 points$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Fourteen different tiles from 147, 258 and 369 in three different suits and the honors. All nine suited tiles add Knitted Straight; a self-drawn win adds Fully Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.lowe: $(bold)Lower Four$()$(br)12 points$(br2)Only 1, 2, 3 and 4. Not counted: No Honors. Only 1, 2 and 3 counts Lower Tiles instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.meld: $(bold)Melded Hand$()$(br)6 points$(br2)All four melds are chows, pungs or melded kongs, and the pair is completed on another player’s discard. Not counted: Single Wait.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.mixe: $(bold)Mixed Shifted Chows$()$(br)6 points$(br2)A chow in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo whose starting numbers rise by one.
$(bold)Mixed Shifted Pungs$()$(br)8 points$(br2)A pung in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo, each number one higher.
$(bold)Mixed Straight$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Chows 123, 456 and 789, each in a different suit.
$(bold)Mixed Triple Chow$()$(br)8 points$(br2)A chow of the same numbers in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo. Two of them do not count Mixed Double Chow.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.name: 16 to 6 Points
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.out_: $(bold)Out with Replacement Tile$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Win by drawing the replacement tile after a kong. Not counted: Self-Drawn. A tile drawn to replace a flower does not count.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.pure: $(bold)Pure Shifted Chows$()$(br)16 points$(br2)Three chows in one suit whose starting numbers rise by one or by two.
$(bold)Pure Straight$()$(br)16 points$(br2)123, 456 and 789 of one suit. These chows do not count Short Straight or Two Terminal Chows.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.reve: $(bold)Reversible Tiles$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Only tiles that look the same upside down: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 of Circles, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 9 of Bamboo, and White. Not counted: One Voided Suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.robb: $(bold)Robbing the Kong$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Win on the tile another player adds to a pung to make a kong. Not counted: Last Tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.thre: $(bold)Three Concealed Pungs$()$(br)16 points$(br2)Three concealed pungs (including concealed kongs); a pung completed with another player’s discard counts as melded. Not counted: Two Concealed Pungs.
$(bold)Three-Suited Terminal Chows$()$(br)16 points$(br2)123 and 789 in each of two suits, with a pair of 5s in the third. Not counted: All Chows, Mixed Double Chow, Two Terminal Chows, No Honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.trip: $(bold)Triple Pung$()$(br)16 points$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of the same number in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo. Two of them do not count Double Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.two_: $(bold)Two Concealed Kongs$()$(br)8 points$(br2)Two concealed kongs. They do not count Concealed Kong or Two Concealed Pungs.
$(bold)Two Dragon Pungs$()$(br)6 points$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of two dragons. They do not count Dragon Pung.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_fan_middle.uppe: $(bold)Upper Four$()$(br)12 points$(br2)Only 6, 7, 8 and 9. Not counted: No Honors. Only 7, 8 and 9 counts Upper Tiles instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.calls: A chow uses only the previous player’s discard; pungs and melded kongs can use any player’s discard. When several players claim the same tile, a win beats a pung or kong, and a pung or kong beats a chow. If several players win on one tile, the first in turn order after the discarder wins.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.calls.cont: After a kong, draw a replacement from the back of the wall. Another player’s added kong can be robbed by winning on the added tile; a concealed kong cannot be robbed.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.name: Flowers and Play
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.tiles: Mahjong Competition Rules (MCR) is played by four players with 136 ordinary tiles and eight flowers, 144 in all. Each player is dealt 13 tiles and the dealer 14; the dealer discards first, and play continues counterclockwise.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.tiles.cont: After the deal, flowers are replaced starting with the dealer: one player reveals every flower in hand and draws replacements from the back of the wall before the next player begins.
A flower drawn during play is revealed and replaced from the back of the wall, again if the replacement is another flower. Flowers never form melds.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_flow.winning: A regular winning hand has four melds and a pair. Seven Pairs, Thirteen Orphans, Lesser and Greater Honors and Knitted Tiles and Knitted Straight have their own shapes; see $(l:mcr_special)Hands and Combining$(/l).$(br2)A win needs at least 8 points from scoring patterns. Flower points do not count toward these 8.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_scoring.match: Everyone starts at zero. A match covers the East, South, West and North rounds, sixteen hands in all. The deal passes after every hand, even when the dealer wins or the hand is drawn.$(br2)If the wall runs out without a win, the hand is a draw and nothing is paid; points already paid for false wins in that hand remain.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_scoring.minimum: A win adds up the points of its scoring patterns. Once the hand has 8 points, each flower adds 1 more, and the total is the hand value. For example, 7 points with two flowers cannot win, but 8 points with two flowers can, for a hand value of 10.

The win button only means the hand has a winning shape, not that it reaches 8 points. Declaring a win below 8 points is a false win: the player pays each of the other three 10 points and cannot win for the rest of the hand, but keeps drawing, discarding and calling as usual.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_scoring.name: Scoring and Payments
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_scoring.payment: On a self-drawn win, each of the other three players pays the winner 8 points plus the hand value. On a discard win, the discarder pays 8 points plus the hand value, and the other two players pay 8 points each.

Example: with a hand value of 10, a self-drawn win collects 18 from each player, 54 in all; a discard win collects 18 from the discarder and 8 from each of the others, 34 in all. MCR has no dealer bonus.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.combini: Patterns that can combine are added together. A pattern whose conditions are already part of a larger pattern is not counted again, and the same tiles cannot be regrouped to count twice.
When scoring sequence-combination patterns, a sequence not yet used in a combination may be combined once with one suitable sequence from an already counted combination.

For example, Mixed Triple Chow cannot also count Mixed Double Chow, and the sequences of a Pure Straight cannot count Short Straight or Two Terminal Chows. When a hand can be divided in several ways, only the highest-scoring division counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.example: Knitted Straight: 147, 258 and 369 in three suits, plus a meld and a pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.knitted: Lesser Honors and Knitted Tiles is fourteen different tiles taken from 147 of one suit, 258 of another, 369 of the third and the honors, without forming melds. With all seven honors it becomes Greater Honors and Knitted Tiles. Both can only be formed with a closed hand.
A Knitted Straight is the nine tiles 147, 258 and 369 in three different suits, plus one meld and a pair. Only that meld may be melded from discards.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.kongs: Kong patterns depend on the number of kongs and whether they are concealed: one melded kong is Melded Kong for 1 point, one concealed kong is Concealed Kong for 2, two melded kongs are Two Melded Kongs for 4, one of each scores 6, and two concealed kongs are Two Concealed Kongs for 8.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.kongs.c: See $(l:mcr_fan_high#three_kongs)Three Kongs$(/l) and $(l:mcr_fan_high#four_kongs)Four Kongs$(/l) for their point values and how they combine with concealed-kong and concealed-pung patterns.
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.name: Hands and Combining
manual.mchjong.entry.mcr_special.pairs: Seven Pairs consists of seven pairs; four identical tiles can count as two pairs. Thirteen Orphans holds one of each of the thirteen terminals and honors plus a second copy of one of them as the pair. Both can only be formed with a closed hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.leaving: With only one human player, click Exit on the toolbar at any time to end the match. With several human players, Exit starts a vote, and the match ends only if everyone agrees. The match and its clocks pause during the vote; no reply does not count as agreement.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.name: Results and Replays
manual.mchjong.entry.results.replays: Click Replays on the toolbar or in the lobby, or type /mchjong replays in chat, to open records of matches you played. After choosing one, drag the timeline, step through or play it, jump to each decision and switch the seat you are watching.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.replays.con: Replay JSON files are exported to replays/mchjong in the game directory. Riichi mahjong replays use Tenhou format only with the default award selection. Selecting a custom award set or disabling a built-in yaku requires MChjong's native replay format. Replays of other variants also use the native format.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.settlement: After each hand, the results screen lists the winner’s scoring patterns and every player’s score change. Riichi mahjong also shows han and fu, and when several players win on one discard you can switch between them. Click a pattern to read its explanation and open its page in this manual.
Click Continue when you are done; the next hand begins once everyone has confirmed.
manual.mchjong.entry.results.sticks: Ordinary mahjong tables use physical point sticks for settlement. To pay points, aim at the point-stick drawer on your side of the table and press Use. Drag the required point sticks into the row for the player who should receive them.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.calls: Chi uses the previous player’s discard to complete a sequence, pon uses any player’s discard to complete a triplet, and an open kan uses any player’s discard to complete a quad. When several players claim the same tile, ron beats pon and kan, and pon and kan beat chi. Discard after a chi or pon.
Chi, pon and open kans make the hand open: yaku marked Closed hand only no longer count, and yaku marked Reduced by 1 han when open lose one han. Concealed kans keep the hand closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.deposi: Mahjong Soul and Tenhou require at least 1,000 points to declare riichi, with at least four drawable tiles left, or three in three-player Riichi mahjong. M.League and JPML A require one drawable tile; WRC allows riichi with none left. M.League, JPML A and WRC all allow riichi with fewer than 1,000 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.furite: If any of your discards is one of your waits, you are in discard furiten and cannot ron on any winning tile. Passing up a ron puts you in temporary furiten until it clears. Passing up a ron after riichi keeps you in furiten for the rest of the hand. You can still win by tsumo, and a red Furiten marker shows the state.

Under Mahjong Soul and WRC rules, temporary furiten clears on your next draw; under the other presets, it clears when you discard after drawing. Under WRC rules, your own chi, pon or open kan also clears it, and passing a winning tile while in tenpai without yaku also causes temporary furiten.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.kans: Four identical tiles in the hand allow a concealed kan. After calling pon, drawing the fourth matching tile allows an added kan. After a kan, draw a replacement from the dead wall. Rules with kan dora also reveal a new dora indicator; Mahjong Soul and Tenhou delay the indicator for open and added kans until the player's discard.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.kans.c: When another player adds a fourth tile to an exposed triplet, the added tile can be claimed for ron if the hand qualifies. Mahjong Soul also allows robbing a concealed kan for Kokushi Musou. Four-player Riichi mahjong allows four replacement draws; three-player Riichi mahjong allows eight, shared by kans and North extraction.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.name: Calls, Riichi and Furiten
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_calls.riichi: With a closed hand in tenpai, discard a tile and deposit 1,000 points to declare riichi. Afterward the hand cannot change: apart from winning, concealed kans and North extraction, discard every tile you draw.
A concealed kan after riichi cannot change the waits. M.League, JPML A and WRC rules also forbid changing the hand's meld composition. JPML A rules additionally forbid losing an existing yaku.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.dealer: The dealer repeats after winning. After an exhaustive draw, the dealer repeats if in tenpai; otherwise the next player deals. After a nondealer wins, the player after the dealer deals.
A dealer repeat or draw adds one honba; a nondealer win resets it. Each honba adds 300 points to a ron and 100 points from each payer to a tsumo. All riichi sticks on the table go to the next winner.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.draws: If the wall runs out without a win, the hand is an exhaustive draw. Players not in tenpai pay those in tenpai 3,000 points in total in a four-player game: with one player in tenpai, the other three pay 1,000 each; with two, the two others pay 1,500 each; with three, the remaining player pays 3,000, shared among them.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.draws.c: Nothing is paid if everyone or no one is in tenpai.$(br2)Under Tenhou rules, a hand counts as tenpai even if all copies of its waits are in the player’s own melds or concealed kans.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.length: A match is a hanchan of East and South rounds by default, with four dealer turns per round; dealer repeats add hands. Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules can shorten it to an East-only match. Endings such as bankruptcy, agari yame and extra rounds depend on the preset; see $(l:riichi_presets)Rule Presets$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.name: Playing a Hand
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.tiles: Four-player Riichi mahjong uses the three suits of Characters, Circles and Bamboo and the seven honors East, South, West, North, White, Green and Red, four of each for 136 tiles. Flowers are not used.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.tiles.c: Each player is dealt 13 tiles and the dealer takes one more. Starting with the dealer, players draw and discard in counterclockwise order. The last 14 tiles of the wall form the dead wall, which supplies kan replacement tiles and dora indicators and is not drawn from normally.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.winning: A standard winning hand has four melds and a pair. Without quads it contains 14 tiles; each quad adds one to the total, including tiles set aside after calls or concealed kans. Three consecutive tiles of one suit form a sequence, three identical tiles a triplet, and four identical tiles declared as a kan a quad.

Two identical tiles form the pair. Honors cannot form sequences, but they can form pairs, triplets or quads. Chiitoitsu and Kokushi Musou use different winning shapes, described in their entries. Winning on a tile drawn by the winner is tsumo; winning on another player's discard is ron.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_flow.yaku: A win needs at least one han from yaku. Dora, Red Dora and North Dora add han but do not count as yaku. Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules can raise the minimum to two or four han, still counting only yaku; under Tenhou rules, Ippatsu does not count toward the minimum either. Yakuman are not affected by the minimum.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.dora: Dora is the tile type following the indicator in a cycle: 1 to 9 in each suit; East, South, West, North for winds; White, Green, Red for dragons. Each cycle wraps back to its first tile. Every dora in the winning hand adds one han, including tiles in called melds. Each red five also adds one han; both bonuses can apply to one tile.
Rules with ura dora reveal its indicators after a riichi win; rules with kan dora reveal additional indicators after kans. JPML A uses neither. Red fives replace the prescribed number of ordinary fives of the same suits without changing the total tile count.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.fu: A regular hand starts with 20 fu. A closed ron adds 10 fu and a tsumo adds 2. Triplets of 2 to 8 score 2 fu open and 4 concealed; quads score 8 open and 16 concealed. Terminals and honors score double. A triplet completed by ron counts as open.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.fu.co: A yakuhai pair adds 2 fu. A double-wind pair adds 4 fu under Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules, or 2 fu under M.League, JPML A and WRC rules. Edge, closed and single waits add 2 fu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.fu_ro: Total fu are rounded up to a multiple of 10. Pinfu tsumo is fixed at 20 fu without the tsumo bonus, and Chiitoitsu is fixed at 25 fu without rounding. An open hand with nothing beyond the base 20 fu counts as 30 fu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.limit: Five han, or 2,000 base points, is a mangan: 8,000 points for a nondealer ron and 12,000 for a dealer ron. Six to seven han is haneman, eight to ten baiman and eleven to twelve sanbaiman, worth 1.5, 2 and 3 times a mangan. M.League and WRC rules round 4 han 30 fu and 3 han 60 fu up to mangan.
Thirteen or more han is a counted yakuman worth four mangan. M.League rules do not use counted yakuman; such hands score sanbaiman at most.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.name: Fu and Scoring
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_points.point: Below mangan, the base points are fu × 2^(han + 2). On a ron, the discarder pays a nondealer four times the base points and a dealer six times. On a nondealer tsumo, the dealer pays twice the base points and each other nondealer once; on a dealer tsumo, each player pays twice. Each payment is rounded up to 100 points.

Example: a nondealer with 3 han 40 fu has 1,280 base points, earning 5,200 by ron, or 2,600 from the dealer and 1,300 from each other player by tsumo. A nondealer’s 2-han Chiitoitsu by ron earns 1,600.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.abor: Online presets have these abortive draws:$(li)Nine terminals: on your first draw with no calls made, you may abort while holding nine or more different terminals and honors.

$(li)Four winds: all four players discard the same wind in the first turn with no calls.$(li)Four riichi: all four players declare riichi.$(li)Four kans: four kans are split between two or more players.

After the fourth kan, a win on its replacement and any ron on the next discard are resolved before the four-kan draw is checked. If one player owns all four kans, play continues. Abortive draws have no noten payments; the dealer repeats and one honba is added.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.choi: Riichi mahjong has seven rule presets: Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules, each for four and three players, plus M.League, JPML A and WRC rules. Below, Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules are called online presets and the other three competition presets.
Online presets can change whether All Simples counts with calls (kuitan), the number of Red Fives, the minimum han and the match length. Changing any other rule adds (Custom) to the preset name.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.comp: Competition presets use no bankruptcy, abortive draws, Nagashi Mangan, agari yame or extra rounds. When several players ron on one tile, only the first in turn order after the discarder wins (head bump).
M.League rules use three Red Fives and give leftover riichi sticks to first place. JPML A and WRC rules use no Red Fives and leave leftover sticks undistributed. WRC rules use Blessing of Man.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.floa: Under JPML A rules, the number of players finishing with 30,000 points or more sets the bonuses for first to fourth place:$(li)0 or 4 players: 0/0/0/0$(li)1 player: +12/−1/−3/−8$(li)2 players: +8/+4/−4/−8$(li)3 players: +8/+3/+1/−12

Under competition presets, players tied on final points share the bonuses and oka of the places they occupy; M.League rules distribute leftover hundreds from the first dealer onward. Online presets break ties by seat order from the first dealer.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.name: Rule Presets
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.onli: Online presets use bankruptcy: the match ends as soon as a player falls below zero; exactly zero continues. If the dealer would repeat in the last hand while in first place with the target score, the match ends instead (agari yame and tenpai yame).

If first place is below the target when the last hand ends, an extra round begins and ends with the hand in which someone reaches it, for at most one round. The target is 30,000 points for four players and 40,000 for three.
Mahjong Soul rules allow several players to ron on one discard; under Tenhou rules, a triple ron is a draw. Riichi sticks left at the end go to first place.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.pao: If your discard lets another player pon or open-kan their third dragon set or fourth wind set, you are liable for Daisangen or Daisuushii. Competition presets also apply liability to a fourth kan completed by an open kan.
If the winner wins by tsumo, the liable player pays that yakuman in full. If a third player deals in, the liable player and the discarder pay half each. Under Tenhou rules, when a liable yakuman combines with another yakuman, the whole hand is settled as liable. Under JPML A and WRC rules, the discarder pays the honba in liability cases.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_presets.scor: At the end of a match, each player’s result is (final points − return) ÷ 1,000 plus the placement bonus. The difference between the return and the starting points of all players, called oka, goes to first place.
$(li)Mahjong Soul rules: four players start with 25,000 and return 25,000, bonuses +15/+5/−5/−15; three players start with 35,000 and return 35,000, bonuses +15/0/−15.
$(li)Tenhou rules: four players start with 25,000 and return 30,000, bonuses +20/+10/−10/−20; three players start with 35,000 and return 40,000, bonuses +20/0/−20.
$(li)M.League rules: start with 25,000 and return 30,000, bonuses +30/+10/−10/−30.$(li)WRC rules: start and return 30,000, bonuses +15/+5/−5/−15.

$(li)JPML A rules: starting and return points are both 30,000, with no oka. The placement bonuses depend on how many players finish with at least 30,000 points; see $(l:riichi_presets#floating)JPML A Placement Bonuses$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.name: Three-Player Mahjong
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.north: A North tile can stay in your hand as an ordinary tile, or you can extract it: set it aside and draw a replacement from the dead wall. Each extracted North adds one han of North Dora, which does not count as a yaku.
Extracting North keeps the hand closed but breaks Ippatsu; a tsumo on its replacement also scores Rinshan Kaihou.$(br2)When another player extracts North, a player waiting on North can ron on it, even without Kokushi Musou. North extraction and kans share the limit of eight replacement tiles.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.paymen: On a tsumo, the other two players pay according to their dealer or nondealer roles in four-player Riichi mahjong. They do not cover the absent fourth player's payment. A nondealer mangan tsumo collects 4,000 points from the dealer and 2,000 points from the other nondealer.
After an exhaustive draw, the noten payments total 2,000 points: with one player in tenpai, the other two pay 1,000 each; with two in tenpai, the third pays 2,000, shared between them.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_sanma.tiles: Three-player mahjong omits the 2 to 8 of Characters, leaving 108 tiles, and does not allow chi. The three players sit East, South and West, and each round has three dealer turns. Each player is dealt 13 tiles and the dealer 14.
When the 1 of Characters is a dora indicator, the dora is the 9 of Characters, and vice versa.$(br2)Players start with 35,000 points. The return is 35,000 points under Mahjong Soul rules and 40,000 under Tenhou rules.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.chankan: $(bold)Chankan$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by ron on the fourth tile another player adds to an exposed triplet. Under Mahjong Soul rules, a Kokushi Musou wait can also rob a concealed kan.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.chanta: $(bold)Chanta$()$(br)2 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Every meld and the pair include a terminal or honor, with at least one sequence and at least one honor.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.chiitoi: $(bold)Chiitoitsu$()$(br)2 han$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Seven different pairs; four identical tiles cannot be two pairs.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.chinits: $(bold)Chinitsu$()$(br)6 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Only one suit with no honors. Chinitsu supersedes Honitsu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.double_: $(bold)Double Riichi$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Declare riichi on your first discard before anyone has called, then win. Double Riichi supersedes Riichi.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.haitei_: $(bold)Haitei Raoyue$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by tsumo on the last normally drawable tile of the wall. Replacement tiles are not the last tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.honitsu: $(bold)Honitsu$()$(br)3 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Only one suit plus honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.honrout: $(bold)Honroutou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Only terminals and honors. With four melds and a pair, Toitoi also counts; in the seven-pairs shape, Chiitoitsu also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.houtei_: $(bold)Houtei Raoyui$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Ron on the discard made after the last tile is drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.iipeiko: $(bold)Iipeikou$()$(br)1 han$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Two identical sequences of the same suit and numbers. Ryanpeikou supersedes Iipeikou.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.intro: This chapter lists the regular yaku. The value under each name is that yaku’s own han; yaku marked Reduced by 1 han when open lose one han with calls, and yaku marked Closed hand only do not count with calls.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.intro.c: A hand’s total is the han of all its yaku plus its dora. Yakuman and limit hands are covered in $(l:riichi_points)Fu and Scoring$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.ippatsu: $(bold)Ippatsu$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win after riichi before your next discard, with no chi, pon, kan or North extraction by anyone in between. JPML A rules do not use Ippatsu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.ittsu: $(bold)Ittsu$()$(br)2 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Sequences 123, 456 and 789 of one suit.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.junchan: $(bold)Junchan$()$(br)3 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)Every meld and the pair include a 1 or 9, with at least one sequence and no honors. Junchan supersedes Chanta.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.menzen_: $(bold)Menzen Tsumo$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by tsumo with a closed hand. Concealed kans keep the hand closed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.nagashi: $(bold)Nagashi Mangan$()$(br)Mangan$(br2)Mahjong Soul and Tenhou rules only. At an exhaustive draw, all your discards are terminals or honors and none was called.
Mahjong Soul rules also require no calls of your own; Tenhou rules allow them. Paid as a mangan tsumo instead of noten payments, without honba or riichi sticks.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.name: Yaku
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.pinhu: $(bold)Pinfu$()$(br)1 han$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)All four melds are sequences, the pair is not yakuhai, and the hand wins on a two-sided wait. It also counts by tsumo.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.renhou: $(bold)Blessing of Man$()$(br)Mangan$(br2)WRC rules only. A nondealer wins by ron before their first draw, with no calls by anyone. The higher of mangan and the normal score counts; scored as mangan, it counts no other yaku or dora.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.riichi: $(bold)Riichi$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Declare riichi with a closed hand in tenpai by discarding a tile and depositing 1,000 points, then win. Double Riichi supersedes Riichi.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.rinshan: $(bold)Rinshan Kaihou$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Win by tsumo on the replacement tile after a kan. In three-player Riichi mahjong, a tsumo on the replacement after North extraction also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.ryanpei: $(bold)Ryanpeikou$()$(br)3 han$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Two Iipeikou plus a pair. Ryanpeikou supersedes Iipeikou and Chiitoitsu.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.sananko: $(bold)Sanankou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Three concealed triplets (including concealed quads). A triplet completed by ron is not concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.sanshok: $(bold)Sanshoku Doujun$()$(br)2 han$(br)Reduced by 1 han when open$(br2)A sequence with the same numbers in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo.
$(bold)Sanshoku Doukou$()$(br)2 han$(br2)A triplet (including quads) with the same number in each of Characters, Circles and Bamboo.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.shousan: $(bold)Shousangen$()$(br)2 han$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of two dragons with the third dragon as the pair. The two dragon sets also score yakuhai, so the hand has at least 4 han.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.toitoi: $(bold)Toitoi$()$(br)2 han$(br2)All four melds are triplets (including quads).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yaku.yakuhai: $(bold)Yakuhai$()$(br)1 han$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of the round wind, your seat wind or a dragon (White, Green or Red), each worth 1 han. A tile that is both the round and seat wind counts both, for 2 han.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.chih: $(bold)Chiihou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)A nondealer wins by tsumo on their first draw before anyone has called.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.chin: $(bold)Chinroutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only 1s and 9s, with all four melds triplets (including quads).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.chuu: $(bold)Pure Chuuren Poutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Before the win, the hand is exactly one suit’s 1112345678999 and can win on any tile from 1 to 9 of that suit. Pure Chuuren Poutou supersedes Chuuren Poutou.
$(bold)Chuuren Poutou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)One suit’s 1112345678999 plus any other tile of that suit. Kans are not allowed.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.dais: $(bold)Daisangen$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of White, Green and Red.
$(bold)Daisuushii$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of East, South, West and North.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.intr: Yakuman do not add regular yaku or dora. When one hand has several yakuman, their values add up. Mahjong Soul rules count Kokushi Musou Thirteen-Sided Wait, Suuankou Tanki, Pure Chuuren Poutou and Daisuushii as double yakuman; other rules count them once.
Daisangen and Daisuushii carry liability rules; see $(l:riichi_presets)Rule Presets$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.koku: $(bold)Kokushi Musou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)One of each of the thirteen terminals and honors, with a second copy of one of them as the pair.

$(bold)Kokushi Musou Thirteen-Sided Wait$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Before the win, the hand holds one of each of the thirteen terminals and honors and can win on any of them. Kokushi Musou Thirteen-Sided Wait supersedes Kokushi Musou.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.name: Yakuman
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.ryuu: $(bold)Ryuuiisou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8 of Bamboo and Green; Green is not required.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.shou: $(bold)Shousuushii$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Triplets (including quads) of three winds with the fourth wind as the pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.suua: $(bold)Suuankou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br)Closed hand only$(br2)Four concealed triplets (including concealed quads). With a dual-pon wait it counts only by tsumo, because a triplet completed by ron is not concealed.
$(bold)Suuankou Tanki$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Four concealed triplets (including quads) are complete, and the hand wins on a single wait for the pair; ron also counts. Suuankou Tanki supersedes Suuankou.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.suuk: $(bold)Suukantsu$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Four quads, open or concealed. The yakuman counts only when the hand wins after the fourth kan.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.tenh: $(bold)Tenhou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)The dealer wins with the dealt hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.riichi_yakuman.tsuu: $(bold)Tsuuiisou$()$(br)Yakuman$(br2)Only honors, and the seven-pairs shape also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.invite: The host can click Invite Player in the lobby sidebar or type /mchjong invite <player> in chat. Invitations expire after 60 seconds. Without invitation teleporting, approach within six blocks of the table's center before accepting. Acceptance seats you directly when a seat is available.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.invite.cont: With invitation teleporting enabled, you can accept from farther away. After arriving beside the table, sit down to join.$(br2)Computer players can fill empty seats. Riichi mahjong offers Easy and Hard computer players; MCR, Sichuan mahjong and Taiwanese mahjong each offer one difficulty level.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.lobby: Aim at an empty mahjong stool and press Use (right-click by default) to sit down. The first player seated becomes the host. Sitting down opens the table's lobby.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.lobby.conti: The host chooses the variant in the lobby sidebar and selects a rule preset, the number of players and other rules under Match Settings. Hover over a rule to read its description. Changing the rules clears every player’s ready status.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.name: Starting a Match
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.start: When every seat is filled, the host clicks Assign Seats and Continue or Draw Winds and Continue. An automatic table assigns seats directly; at an ordinary table, each player draws a face-down wind tile to decide the seats.
manual.mchjong.entry.seating.start.conti: Each player then sits in the assigned seat and clicks Ready. Automatic Reseating, on by default, moves you to your seat. The match starts when everyone is ready and the equipment meets the selected rules; Table Preparation lists anything missing.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.all_pun: $(bold)All Pungs$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Four pungs (including kongs) and a pair. Seven pairs does not count All Pungs.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.base: Fan set the base points: 1 point for 0 fan, 2 for 1 fan, 4 for 2 fan and 8 for 3 fan. By default the cap is 3 fan, so more fan still score 8. A win with no fan pattern is a Basic Hand worth 0 fan.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.base.co: On a discard win, the discarder pays the base points. On a self-drawn win, each other player still in the hand pays the base points plus 1.

Example: Full Flush is 2 fan, so a discard win collects 4 points. A self-drawn win with all four players in the hand collects 5 from each of the other three, 15 in all; if one player has already won and left, it collects from the remaining two, 10 in all.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.full_fl: $(bold)Full Flush$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Only one suit. It adds to Seven Pairs, Root, All Pungs and other fan, scored after the cap.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.golden_: $(bold)Golden Single Wait$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)After four melds are pung (including kongs), one tile remains in hand and wins as a single wait for the pair. All Pungs also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.kong: $(bold)Kong$()$(br)1 fan each$(br2)MIL SBR 2025 only: each declared kong scores 1 fan. These fan are separate from the kong payment collected when the kong was declared.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.name: Fan and Base Points
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.robbing: $(bold)Robbing a Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win on the tile another player adds to a pung to make a kong; the pung stays. Under T/TFMJ 01—2024, it also covers an added kong made with a kong’s replacement tile. Win on a Discard after a Kong does not also count.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.root: $(bold)Root$()$(br)1 fan each$(br2)Each set of all four copies of a tile in the winning hand scores 1 fan. Under MIL SBR 2025, four tiles already declared as a kong count as Kong instead; under T/TFMJ 01—2024, both count as Root (including Kongs).
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.seven_p: $(bold)Seven Pairs$()$(br)2 fan$(br2)Seven pairs with no melds. Four identical tiles can form two pairs and also count a Root. All Pungs does not count.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.shoot_a: $(bold)Win on a Discard after a Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win on the discard another player makes after a kong. Under MIL SBR 2025, it also covers winning on an added kong made with a kong’s replacement tile; that kong stands but collects no kong payment.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.under_t: $(bold)Last-Tile Win$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win by drawing the last tile of the wall, or on the discard made after that draw. It does not count in the ready check at an exhaustive draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_fan.win_aft: $(bold)Win after Kong$()$(br)1 fan$(br2)Win by drawing the replacement tile after a kong. The fan count first; then each payer adds 1 point for the self-draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.battle: Sichuan mahjong is played as Blood Battle: a player who wins leaves the hand, and the others keep drawing and discarding until three players have won or the wall runs out. Several players can win on the same discard, and the discarder pays each of them.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.dealer: The first player to win a hand deals the next one; if the first win was several players winning on the same discard, the discarder deals. If nobody wins, the dealer stays. Both presets play eight hands and rank players by total points.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.exampl: Four identical tiles as two pairs, which also scores a Root.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.name: Voids and Blood Battle
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.passin: Passing a win on another player’s discard puts you under a passed-win restriction: you cannot win on a discard for the same or lower fan, comparing fan after the cap. Discarding a tile you could have won on also starts the restriction.
It ends on your next draw or when your hand is no longer ready. The restriction does not affect self-drawn wins.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.tiles: Sichuan mahjong is played by four players with only the suits of Characters, Circles and Bamboo, four of each tile for 108 tiles; there are no honors or flowers. Each player is dealt 13 tiles and the dealer 14, and the dealer discards first. Chi is not allowed; only pung and kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.void: After the deal, each player chooses a void suit from Characters, Circles and Bamboo and must discard every tile of that suit before winning. While you hold tiles of your void suit, you can discard only those tiles, and you cannot pung or kong them.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.void.c: Under MIL SBR 2025, each player also secretly picks the first void-suit tile to discard and must discard it on their first turn; a player with no tiles of that suit picks none. The void suits are revealed together once everyone has chosen, but the chosen tiles stay hidden.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_flow.winnin: A winning hand is four melds and a pair, or seven pairs; four identical tiles can form two pairs. There is no minimum fan, so a 0-fan hand can win, but a hand still holding void-suit tiles cannot.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_payments.dr: When the wall runs out, the players who have not won are checked for readiness. Each player who is not ready pays every ready player the highest base points their hand could reach, ignoring timing-based fan such as Win after Kong and Last-Tile Win.
Players who already won take no part. A player who is not ready also refunds any kong payments not yet transferred.

Example: one player has already won. Of the remaining three, one is not ready and two have ready hands worth at most 2 and 8 base points. The unready player pays them 2 and 8 points respectively.$(br2)A hand that ends with three winners has no ready check or kong refund.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_payments.fl: A player who still holds void-suit tiles at an exhaustive draw is a passive flower pig, treated as not ready, and refunds kong payments. A player who breaks the void-suit rule becomes an active flower pig:

24 competition points are deducted at once and paid to no one, the player can no longer win, collects nothing in the ready check and refunds kong payments, but also pays nothing in the ready check if already ready.
The host can change the fan cap, self-draw bonus, kong payments, active flower pig penalty and number of hands in the rule settings.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_payments.ko: A kong is paid immediately, separately from fan at the win:$(li)Concealed kong: each other player still in the hand pays 2 points.$(li)Kong on a discard: the discarder pays 2 points.

$(li)Added kong: adding the fourth tile to a pung immediately after drawing it collects 1 point from each other player still in the hand; adding it later collects nothing.$(br2)A kong grants a replacement tile. If it is robbed, the original pung remains; the added kong does not stand or earn points.

MIL SBR 2025 treats an added kong made with a kong replacement tile differently: if another player wins on that tile, it counts as a win after a kong discard. The added kong stands but earns no kong points. T/TFMJ 01-2024 still treats this as robbing the kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_payments.sh: When a discard after a kong is won on, the kong payments are handled separately. MIL SBR 2025 refunds only the last kong’s payments, each payer taking back what they paid. T/TFMJ 01—2024 transfers all the kong payments from that chain of kongs to the winner instead.

Example: under T/TFMJ 01—2024, a player collects 5 points from consecutive kongs, then makes a discard claimed by two winners. Each winner receives 3 points, with the discarder supplying the missing point. These transfers are separate from win payments and are not refunded after a draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_presets.com: Sichuan mahjong has two rule presets, MIL SBR 2025 and T/TFMJ 01—2024.

Both cap fan at 3, add 1 point for self-draws, pay 2 points for concealed kongs and kongs on discards and 1 for added kongs, deduct 24 points for an active flower pig, play eight hands and make players who are not ready refund kong payments at a draw. Neither uses tile exchange.
manual.mchjong.entry.sichuan_presets.dif: The presets differ as follows:$(li)First discard: MIL SBR 2025 picks the first void-suit discard when choosing the void suit; T/TFMJ 01—2024 does not.

$(li)Kongs and roots: MIL SBR 2025 scores declared kongs as Kong and undeclared sets of four as Root; T/TFMJ 01—2024 scores both as Root (including Kongs).$(li)Discards after kongs: MIL SBR 2025 refunds only the last kong; T/TFMJ 01—2024 transfers the kong payments to the winner.

$(li)Added kong after a kong: MIL SBR 2025 treats a win on it as Win on a Discard after a Kong; T/TFMJ 01—2024 treats it as Robbing a Kong.$(li)Walls: MIL SBR 2025 builds 14 stacks for East and West; T/TFMJ 01—2024 for South and North.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.intro: Riichi mahjong on an ordinary table uses physical dice and point sticks, which must be in a mahjong box beforehand. Automatic tables and the other three variants keep score themselves and need neither.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.intro.continu: Bone meal, white dye and black dye make two dice. A match on an ordinary table needs at least two dice in a box in the table’s storage.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.kit: At the start of a match, the table distributes point sticks from the mahjong boxes into each player's drawer. Each 25,000-point kit contains ten 100-point sticks, four 1,000-point sticks, two 5,000-point sticks and one 10,000-point stick.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.kit.continued: Compared with the 25,000-point kit, a 30,000-point start adds one 5,000-point stick; a 35,000-point start adds one 10,000-point stick.$(br2)Without the bankruptcy rule, each player also needs one bankruptcy stick for paying while below zero.
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.name: Dice and Point Sticks
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.sticks: A bone block in a stonecutter makes 24 blank point sticks. In a crafting table, eight blank sticks and one dye mark all eight with the same value:$(li)White dye: 100 points
manual.mchjong.entry.stock.sticks.contin: $(li)Blue dye: 1,000 points$(li)Yellow dye: 5,000 points$(li)Red dye: 10,000 points$(li)Black dye: a bankruptcy stick (−10,000 points)
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.calls: A chow uses only the previous player’s discard; pungs and open kongs can use any player’s discard. When several players claim the same tile, a win beats a pung or kong, and a pung or kong beats a chow. If several players claim a win, the first in turn order after the discarder wins.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.calls.c: Discard after a chow or pung. Every kong needs a replacement draw. Another player’s added kong can be robbed; a concealed kong cannot.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.example: Five melds and a pair make seventeen tiles.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.flowers: Opening flowers are replaced in turn, starting with the dealer: each player reveals every flower in hand and draws replacements from the back of the wall. A replacement that is another flower waits until all four players have finished that round and is replaced in the next round.
A flower drawn during play is revealed and replaced from the back of the wall until an ordinary tile is drawn.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.name: Tiles, Flowers and Play
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.passing: Passing a win puts you under a passed-win restriction: you cannot win on a discard or by self-draw. Drawing a tile alone does not clear it. It clears when you discard a tile that was not among your waits immediately before that draw or call, or when you complete an added kong. Flower wins are not affected.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.ready: To declare ready, discard a tile that leaves your hand ready. Afterward you cannot chow, pung or kong, and must discard each tile you draw unless you win. Declaring ready is not required to win, but a win after declaring adds the Declared Ready tai.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.reserve: Some tiles at the back of the wall are reserved: sixteen by default, plus one more for each completed kong, or a fixed sixteen if chosen before the match. Reserved tiles cannot be drawn or used to replace flowers or kongs. When no tile can be drawn or replaced, the hand ends in a draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.tiles: Taiwanese mahjong is played by four players. Pocket Common uses 136 ordinary tiles and eight flowers; Southern Common uses no flowers. Each player takes four tiles in each of four dealing rounds. The dealer takes one more, starting with 17 tiles against the other players' 16, and discards first.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_flow.tiles.c: A standard winning hand has five melds and a pair. Without kongs it contains 17 tiles; each kong adds one to the total. Count tiles set aside after calls and concealed kongs, but not exposed flowers.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.amo: $(bold)Calculating Win Payments$()$(br2)Each player's payment is base + tai × points per tai. The base is a fixed number of points included in each payment. By default, the base is 1 point and each tai is worth 1 point.

Add only patterns that can score together. Concealed Self-Draw is 3 tai and replaces separate awards for Concealed Hand and Self-Draw. See $(l:taiwan_tai)Tai Patterns$(/l) for the conditions. Payments involving the dealer also include $(l:taiwan_payments#dealer)Dealer Tai and Repeat Tai$(/l).
The host can change the base, points per tai, dealer tai and tai per repeat under Scoring and Payments in the rule settings.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.dea: $(bold)Dealer Tai and Repeat Tai$()$(br2)For a win on a discard, add dealer tai and repeat tai if either the winner or the discarder is the dealer. If both are nondealers, neither addition applies.
When the dealer self-draws, all three nondealers add dealer tai and repeat tai to their payments. When a nondealer self-draws, only the dealer adds these tai; the other two nondealers do not.
Pocket Common awards 1 dealer tai plus 2 tai for each repeat. One repeat is called 連一拉一 and two repeats 連二拉二. These add 3 tai and 5 tai respectively, including the dealer tai.

Example: under Pocket Common, the dealer has repeated once. A nondealer self-draws for 3 tai, including the self-draw award but excluding dealer and repeat tai. The other nondealers pay 1 + 3 = 4 points each; the dealer pays 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 = 7 points. The winner receives 15 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.flo: $(bold)Flower Wins: Eight Flowers and Seven Robbing One$()$(br2)Pocket Common allows automatic wins based on flower tiles without a standard winning hand of five melds and a pair. A flower win cannot be declined and is not blocked by a passed-win restriction.

$(li)Eight Flowers: holding all eight flowers scores 8 tai, paid by the other three players as a self-draw.$(li)Seven Robbing One: holding seven flowers while another player holds the eighth scores 8 tai, paid only by the holder of that last flower.

During play, drawing a seventh or eighth flower requires completing the flower replacement before checking the flower win. If a player already holds seven flowers when another draws the eighth, Seven Robbing One takes effect immediately. The player drawing the eighth flower does not replace it and pays the winner.
During the initial flower replacement, wait until every player has finished replacing flowers. Flower wins are then checked in turn order, starting with the dealer.

If the replacement also completes a standard winning hand, score its tai separately from the flower win. The standard self-draw is paid by the other three players; the flower win determines its own paying players. A player paying for both includes the base only once. Add dealer and repeat tai according to each player's role.

Example: a nondealer draws a seventh flower and wins on its replacement. The ordinary win totals 5 tai before flower-win and dealer additions. Another nondealer holds the eighth flower; the dealer has not repeated. The flower holder pays 1 + 5 + 8 = 14 points, the dealer pays 1 + 5 + 1 = 7 points, and the remaining nondealer pays 1 + 5 = 6 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.pay: $(bold)Who Pays$()$(br2)For a win on a discard, only the discarder pays the winner. For robbing a kong, the player declaring the added kong pays. For a self-draw, the other three players each pay the winner. An exhaustive draw requires no payments. Declaring a kong earns no points.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.pre: $(bold)Differences Between Pocket Common and Southern Common$()$(br2)Both presets collect common ways of playing; neither is the uniform rule of a region. Southern Common differs from Pocket Common as follows, and its other tai patterns and values are the same:

$(li)It uses 136 tiles without flowers, so it has no flower wins, Seat Flowers or Flower Sets.$(li)Single Wait scores no tai.$(li)The dealer’s own 1 tai is not added, but each repeat still adds 2 tai: 2 tai for one repeat and 4 tai for two.

$(li)Hand tai are capped at 4, so a larger hand counts as 4 tai. Dealer tai and repeat tai are added outside the cap.$(br2)Example: under Southern Common, the dealer has repeated once and self-draws a hand normally worth 8 tai. It counts as 4 tai, and each of the other three players pays 1 + 4 + 2 = 7 points.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.rep: $(bold)Dealer Repeats and the End of the Match$()$(br2)If the dealer wins or the hand ends in an exhaustive draw, the dealer deals again.
This is a dealer repeat, and the repeat count increases by one. If a nondealer wins, the dealer’s next player in turn order becomes dealer and the count returns to zero.

A match has four rounds, East, South, West and North, and each player deals once per round: sixteen dealer positions in all. The fourth North dealer can still repeat; the match ends when that dealer passes the deal. Scores start at zero and accumulate. A negative score does not end the match.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_payments.res: $(bold)Payments on the Results Screen$()$(br2)The results screen lists the winner’s tai patterns and tai, then one line for each player’s payment to the winner, with the base, hand tai and dealer tai in parentheses.
Flower-win tai count as hand tai, and repeat tai count as dealer tai. After an exhaustive draw, the title reads Exhaustive draw and no payments are listed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.all_from: $(bold)All from Others$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)All five melds are chows, pungs or open kongs, and the pair is completed on another player’s discard. Not counted with a concealed kong.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.all_hono: $(bold)All Honors$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Only honors. Not counted: All Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.all_trip: $(bold)All Triplets$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Five pungs (including kongs) and a pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.big_four: $(bold)Big Four Winds$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of East, South, West and North. Round Wind and Seat Wind count separately.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.big_thre: $(bold)Big Three Dragons$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of Red, Green and White. Not counted: Red Dragon, Green Dragon, White Dragon.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.conceale: $(bold)Concealed Hand$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on another player's discard without having called a chow, pung or open kong. Concealed kongs are allowed. A concealed self-drawn win scores Concealed Self-Draw instead; Concealed Hand is not counted.
$(bold)Concealed Self-Draw$()$(br)3 tai$(br2)Concealed only, winning by self-draw. Not counted: Concealed Hand, Self-Draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.declared: $(bold)Declared Ready$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win after declaring ready. Declaring ready does not require a concealed hand. Not counted when Heavenly or Earthly Ready counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.earthly_: $(bold)Earthly Ready$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)A nondealer declares ready on their first discard, before anyone has chowed, punged or konged, and later wins. Not counted: Declared Ready.
$(bold)Earthly Hand$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)A nondealer wins by self-draw on their first draw, before anyone has chowed, punged or konged. Not counted: Concealed Self-Draw, Concealed Hand, Self-Draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.eight_fl: $(bold)Eight Flowers$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)An automatic flower win with all eight flowers; no winning shape is needed. Not counted: Seat Flower, Flower Set. Payment is covered in Payments and Repeats.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.five_con: $(bold)Five Concealed Triplets$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Five concealed pungs (including concealed kongs); a pung completed on another player’s discard is not concealed. Not counted: Four and Three Concealed Triplets. All Triplets also counts.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.flower_s: $(bold)Flower Set$()$(br)1 tai per set$(br2)A complete set of spring, summer, autumn and winter, or of plum, orchid, bamboo and chrysanthemum; each set scores 1 tai. Pocket Common only; not counted with a flower win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.four_con: $(bold)Four Concealed Triplets$()$(br)5 tai$(br2)Four concealed pungs (including concealed kongs); Not counted: Three Concealed Triplets.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.full_flu: $(bold)Full Flush$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Only one suit, with no honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.green_dr: $(bold)Green Dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of Green.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.half_flu: $(bold)Half Flush$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Only one suit plus honors.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.half_fro: $(bold)Half from Others$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)All five melds are chows, pungs or open kongs, and the pair is completed by self-draw.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.heavenly: $(bold)Heavenly Ready$()$(br)16 tai$(br2)The dealer declares ready on their first discard, before anyone has chowed, punged or konged, and later wins. Not counted: Concealed Hand, Declared Ready.

$(bold)Heavenly Hand$()$(br)24 tai$(br2)After replacing flowers, the dealer’s dealt hand is already complete, before anyone has chowed, punged or konged. Not counted: Concealed Self-Draw, Concealed Hand, Self-Draw, Replacement Win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.human_wi: $(bold)Human Hand$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)A nondealer wins on another player’s first discard before the dealer’s second discard, with no chow, pung (including kongs) by anyone. Not counted: Concealed Hand.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.intro: Each value is the tai awarded for that pattern, not the whole hand. Patterns listed as not counted are not added again. See $(l:taiwan_payments)Win Payments and Dealer Repeats$(/l) for dealer tai, repeat tai and scoring limits.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.intro.co: Southern Common does not score Single Wait and caps hand tai at 4; see $(l:taiwan_payments)Payments and Repeats$(/l).
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.last_dis: $(bold)Last Discard$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on the discard made by the player who drew the last drawable tile.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.last_dra: $(bold)Last Draw$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win by self-draw on the last drawable tile. Reserved tiles are not drawable.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.name: Tai Patterns
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.pinfu: $(bold)Pinfu$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Five chows and a suited pair, with no honors or flowers, won on another player’s discard. No two-sided wait is required; Single Wait also counts when it applies.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.red_drag: $(bold)Red Dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of Red.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.replacem: $(bold)Replacement Win$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win by self-draw on a replacement tile. Pocket Common counts replacements for kongs and flowers; Southern Common counts only kong replacements. Apply Self-Draw or Concealed Self-Draw according to their conditions, without counting both.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.robbing_: $(bold)Robbing a Kong$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on the tile another player adds to a pung to make a kong. Concealed kongs cannot be robbed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.round_wi: $(bold)Round Wind$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of the round wind. Round Wind and Seat Wind both count when they are the same wind.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.seat_flo: $(bold)Seat Flower$()$(br)1 tai per flower$(br2)Flower numbers 1 to 4 correspond to East, South, West and North; each flower matching your seat wind scores 1 tai. Pocket Common only; not counted with a flower win.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.seat_win: $(bold)Seat Wind$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of your seat wind. Each hand, seat winds run East, South, West and North from the dealer.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.self_dra: $(bold)Self-Draw$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)Win on a tile you draw yourself. A concealed self-drawn win counts Concealed Self-Draw instead.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.seven_ro: $(bold)Seven Robbing One$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)An automatic flower win when you hold seven flowers and another player holds the last one; no winning shape is needed. Not counted: Seat Flower, Flower Set. Payment is covered in Payments and Repeats.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.single_w: $(bold)Single Wait$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)The whole hand waits on only one kind of tile: edge, closed or single waits all qualify, and that tile need not be the last copy. Not scored under Southern Common.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.small_fo: $(bold)Small Four Winds$()$(br)8 tai$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of three winds with the fourth wind as the pair.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.small_th: $(bold)Small Three Dragons$()$(br)4 tai$(br2)Pungs (including kongs) of two dragons with the third dragon as the pair. Not counted: Red Dragon, Green Dragon, White Dragon.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.three_co: $(bold)Three Concealed Triplets$()$(br)2 tai$(br2)Three concealed pungs (including concealed kongs); A pung completed on another player’s discard is not concealed.
manual.mchjong.entry.taiwan_tai.white_dr: $(bold)White Dragon$()$(br)1 tai$(br2)A pung (including kongs) of White.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.backs: The sixteen vanilla dyes change the color of tile backs. Put a dye in the box’s dye slot and click Dye backs to recolor every tile in the box for one dye. With Undo Dye in the slot, the same button removes the back color.
manual.mchjong.entry.tiles.backs.continu: In a crafting table, one dye can also color a stack of tiles, a mahjong box, a table cloth or a mahjong stool.
